title: Hon’ble Vice President of India to Release “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development
subtitle: Major Thrust to Sustainably Harness the Untapped Potential of Island Resources
body_text:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government of India is organizing an Outreach Programme of Ministry of Fisheries, Govt. of India at Agatti, Lakshadweep on Monday, 31 st August 2026. The Hon’ble Vice President will Release “ Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031 ” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development.
The Outreach Programme will be graced by the august presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj along with Shri Praful Khode Patel, Hon’ble Administrator of Lakshadweep. The event will also witness the participation of ssss fish farmers and fishers including women fish farmers and fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Lakshadweep, representatives from fisheries cluster and line Ministries and Departments.
India’s vast marine resources remain significantly underutilized despite the country’s immense oceanic wealth . With a coastline spanning 11,099 km, an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of 2.2 million sq. km and an estimated marine fisheries potential of 5.31 million tonnes, India possesses tremendous opportunities for sustainable fisheries, deep-sea fishing, mariculture and blue economy development. Lakshadweep exemplifies this untapped potential, with an EEZ of nearly 4 lakh sq. km, accounting for about 17% of India’s total EEZ, and a lagoon area of over 4,200 sq. km. This vast and resource-rich marine ecosystem offers significant scope for harnessing high-value fisheries resources, expanding mariculture, generating coastal livelihoods and accelerating sustainable blue economy growth.
The Government of India is adopting a cluster-based approach to drive integrated and value chain-oriented growth in the fisheries sector. In line with this strategy, Lakshadweep has been notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster to promote cultivation, processing, value addition and market linkages. The Lakshadweep islands are also endowed with abundant marine ornamental fisheries resources, offering significant potential for sustainable rearing, exports and livelihood generation while conserving the marine ecosystems.
During the outreach program, The Hon’ble Vice President will distribute benefits to beneficiaries in fisheries sector and release the Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development. The Strategic Action Plan will provide a uniform framework for scientific management, biosecurity, quality assurance and regulatory compliance across the ornamental fisheries value chain. The SOPs will standardize practices relating to broodstock management, breeding, hatchery operations, production systems, quarantine, health management, traceability, aquarium operations, handling, transport and trade, ensuring consistency and adoption of best management practices nationwide. They will also strengthen stakeholder capacities, improve product quality and biosecurity standards, facilitate certification and market access, and support the sustainable, organized and globally competitive growth of India’s ornamental fisheries sector.
Background
India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of about 24 lakh sq. km. The marine fisheries potential within India’s EEZ is estimated at 58.6 lakh MT, supporting the livelihoods of approximately 50 lakh fishers and contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export revenues. India is presently among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing countries globally and exported seafood valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26.
Most fishing activities are concentrated within 40–50 nautical miles of the coast, while deeper waters and areas beyond national jurisdiction offer substantial opportunities for harvesting high-value species, particularly tuna and tuna-like resources. recognising the strategic importance of sustainable marine fisheries, the Government of India, has notified enabling framework for sustainable harnessing of fisheries from the Indian EEZ and the High Seas including Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels, 2025.
Lakshadweep is endowed with rich oceanic fisheries resources, particularly high-value tuna species such as Yellowfin Tuna and Skipjack Tuna, which form the backbone of the island’s marine fisheries sector. Supported by vast and productive waters, these commercially important species offer significant opportunities for sustainable harvesting, value addition, export growth and livelihood generation, positioning Lakshadweep as a key hub for tuna-based fisheries and blue economy development.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: The Vice President of India released the 'Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031' Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development at an Outreach Programme of the Department of Fisheries held in Agatti, Lakshadweep on 31 August 2026. The plan sets out a uniform national framework covering broodstock management, breeding, hatchery operations, quarantine, health management, traceability, and trade standards for the ornamental fisheries value chain. The event also highlighted Lakshadweep's designation as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster and its untapped marine and tuna fisheries potential as part of India's blue economy push.
enrichment.context: Ornamental fisheries—the breeding and trade of aquarium/decorative fish—is a niche but growing segment of India's fisheries sector with export and livelihood potential, especially in island territories like Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar. Standardizing biosecurity, quarantine, and traceability protocols (as under this plan) is meant to help India's ornamental fish exports meet international quality and health certification requirements, opening market access similar to established exporters like Singapore and Sri Lanka. This initiative fits within the government's broader cluster-based approach to fisheries development under schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), which promotes value-chain integration, and reflects continuing efforts to position India's Exclusive Economic Zone and island territories as strategic assets for blue economy growth, including deep-sea and high-seas fishing under the 2025 High Seas Fishing Guidelines. Lakshadweep's notification as a Seaweed Cluster and its tuna-rich waters are cited as examples of underutilized marine resources that the government intends to harness sustainably for coastal livelihoods.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Lakshadweep's marine resources as highlighted in a recent government release:
1. Lakshadweep's Exclusive Economic Zone accounts for about 17% of India's total EEZ.
2. Lakshadweep has been notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states Lakshadweep's EEZ of nearly 4 lakh sq. km accounts for about 17% of India's total EEZ, and that Lakshadweep has been notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster to promote cultivation, processing and value addition.

prelims_questions.question: 'Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031', mentioned in news, is a strategic action plan related to which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031 is the Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development, providing a framework for scientific management, biosecurity, and regulatory compliance across the ornamental fisheries value chain.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of standardizing biosecurity and quality assurance protocols in India's ornamental fisheries sector for enhancing export competitiveness and rural livelihoods.
India's island territories like Lakshadweep possess vast untapped marine resources. Examine the challenges and opportunities in harnessing this potential for blue economy development.

study_notes.reason: The release's factual core (a newly launched action plan name and a cluster designation) is thin and administrative, while its real value lies in what it signals about India's cluster-based, export-oriented approach to niche fisheries segments and underutilized blue economy resources.

prelims.point: 'Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031' is the Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development launched by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying.
prelims.why_important: A newly named national mission is a natural target for a 'match the scheme with its focus area' question.

prelims.point: Lakshadweep has been notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster under India's cluster-based fisheries development approach.
prelims.why_important: Tests awareness of India's cluster-based value-chain strategy and which region is designated for which fisheries niche.

prelims.point: India notified 'Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels, 2025' to regulate fishing beyond the EEZ.
prelims.why_important: Useful to distinguish India's EEZ-based fisheries regulation from its high-seas fishing framework, a distinction UPSC favours.

mains.point: Standardizing SOPs for broodstock management, breeding, quarantine, health and traceability aims to help India's ornamental fisheries meet international certification norms and gain export market access.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on how regulatory/quality standardization in a niche agri-allied sector can enhance India's competitiveness in global trade.

mains.point: India's cluster-based approach (e.g., Lakshadweep as Seaweed Cluster, ornamental fisheries potential in islands) reflects a strategy of leveraging island territories' underutilized marine resources for blue economy growth and coastal livelihoods.
mains.analytical_use: Can support an answer on strategies to harness India's EEZ and island resources sustainably, or on livelihood diversification in coastal/island communities.
